faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Try the following recommended color correction methods:
Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.
Compare the print result with the image on your computer screen in a well-lit environment. Since monitors and printers produce colors differently, printed colors and screen colors do not always look the same.
If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: I see horizontal or vertical lines in my printout. What should I do?
faqs.answer:

If there are gaps in the nozzle check pattern, clean the print head nozzles.
If there are no gaps in the nozzle check pattern, try the solutions below.
Horizontal Banding
Increase the print resolution.
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Select an alternate paper profile for ink coverage.
Select the correct paper type in the printer driver.
Adjust the paper feed
Vertical Banding
Turn off
Simple Settings
and uncheck the
High Speed
setting in the printer driver.
Align the print head.

faqs.question: I see the message Communication Error when I use a USB connection. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Do the following:
Delete all print jobs in the print queue.
Turn the printer off.
Note:
Make sure the USB cable is connected correctly.
Restart your computer. When the desktop appears, turn your printer on and follow the on-screen instructions.
Note:
If the problem continues, turn the printer off again and delete the printer in the list of printers. Then disconnect the USB cable from the printer and connect it again.

faqs.question: I see the message Service Request 00010004 - 000101D. What should I do?
faqs.answer:
Service Request errors in the range 00010004 - 000101D are related to a carriage movement problem. In some instances like paper jams, the carriage locking tab may be partially pushed in, causing the carriage locking mechanism to put a drag on the carriage or lock the carriage completely. This will cause a carriage error. Make sure the carriage locking tab is pulled to the left. Then turn the printer's power off and release the carriage by pushing down on the cutter blade. Slide the carriage to the left and look for any paper that also may be restricting the carriage from moving freely.
00010004
CR Motor encoder check error
00010005
CR Motor out of step
00010006
CR Motor over current
00010007
CR Motor in-position time-out
0001000A
CR axis detection error
0001000F
CR Motor PWM output faulty
0001001D
CR servo parameter error
The T-Fence may also be dirty or out of the carriage encoder. Check to make sure it is clean and in the center of the encoder. Contact Epson for additional assistance.

faqs.question: How long does it take to switch between black modes on my product?
faqs.answer: Less than ten minutes.

faqs.question: Do the 220ml ink cartridges stick out of the front of my product?
faqs.answer: Yes. The 220ml ink cartridges extend in front of the printer; you need leave the ink compartment cover open.

faqs.question: Why are there only three cartridges in the black ink conversion kit?
faqs.answer: The ink conversion process drains only the black ink channel; the C/M/Y colors are not drained. The three cartridges in the conversion kit are used to close the C/M/Y ink valves during the draining process. However, the process performs an initial fill on the whole ink system after the draining is complete.

faqs.question: Do I need to drain the ink cartridges before transporting my product?
faqs.answer: No. The printer has mechanical ink valves that close when the ink levers are lifted up. For transportation, 110 ml ink cartridges (expended or full) should be installed in each ink slot and both ink levers should be raised to their up position.

faqs.question: Does my product have a pressurized ink delivery system?
faqs.answer: No.

faqs.question: Why is a crease appearing in my roll media?
faqs.answer: A crease in roll media is the result of the paper feed roller holding the media for a long time. Remove the roll media from the paper path when you have finished using it to prevent the media from being creased.

faqs.question: If I don't use roll paper do I need to have the roll paper holder attached?
faqs.answer: No. The printer will work without the roll paper holder installed. The holder is designed to be removed easily.

* Non-Epson roll media widths
The top and bottom edges can be automatically cut to any length.

faqs.question: How can I prevent paper from jamming or misfeeding from the paper tray?
faqs.answer:
Try the following:
Make sure the printer's environment falls within the required temperature and humidity range.
Temperature
Operation
10 to 35°C
(50 to 95°F)
Print quality guarantee
15 to 25°C
(59 to 77°F)
Humidity
(without condensation)
Operation
20 to 80% RH
Print quality guarantee
40 to 60% RH
Make sure the paper (cut sheet only) is not too thick or too thin; 3.15 to 59 mil (0.08 to 1.5 mm)
Make sure no foreign objects are inside the printer.
Make sure the
Media Type
setting in the printer software is correct for the paper you are using.
Make sure the platen gap setting is correct for the paper or media you're printing on. See
Adjusting the Platen Gap for Thick or Thin Paper
.
If you're not using Epson media, make sure you use a paper configuration to adjust for the paper's thickness and drying time.
If you need to add paper to the paper tray, first remove all paper from the tray and then add paper to the removed stack and reload it.
Fan the paper and tap it on a flat surface to even the edges.
If your paper is curled, flatten it before you load it. If it curls excessively and jams frequently, stop using it.
Load the sheets with the printable side face down and the edge of the paper against the right inner corner of the paper tray. Make sure the sheets lie flat on the bottom of the tray.
Don't load paper above the arrow mark inside the edge guide.
Make sure the paper guide and edge guide is snug against the paper.
Store unused sheet media on a flat surface in its original package.

faqs.question: The colors on my printouts do not match the colors on my computer monitor. What should I do?
faqs.answer:

Use ICC profiles during the color management process.
Ensure that you are using the correct output profile for your loaded media.
Note:
You may need to create a custom ICC profile for the best results.
Ensure that your monitor is calibrated and is displaying accurate color.

If the recommendations above do not help, contact Epson support.
The color management process is complex. We can assist you with the proper assignment of settings; however, we cannot assist you with creating a custom color profile.

faqs.question: Why are some of the paper types grayed out?
faqs.answer: The paper path you select determines which media types are available. A media type is grayed out if it can be loaded only in the manual front or rear slot or as roll paper. The driver grays out these media types because feeding them from the paper tray may cause damage to the paper coating.

faqs.question: What does the Common Updater 7.0 file do?
faqs.answer: The Common Updater 7.0 file provides the latest Mac OS X 10.6 support for your printer driver. Before installing the updater, make sure the most current version of the Mac OS X 10.5 or 10.6 printer driver is installed on your computer. Restart your computer after installing the updater.

faqs.question: Can my product switch automatically between Matte Black and Photo Black?
faqs.answer: No. Because Epson UltraChrome K3 Ink technology requires all eight channels to produce both color and black and white prints, there isn't enough room to install both the Matte Black and Photo Black ink cartridges at the same time.

faqs.question: When should I use the product profiles that end in PK and MK?
faqs.answer: Use the PK profile when photo black ink is installed in the printer. Use the MK profile when matte black ink is installed in the printer.

faqs.question: What does the Remote Panel utility do?
faqs.answer:
The EPSON LFP Remote Panel Utility can be used to:
Update firmware
Perform nozzle checks
Run the bi-d and uni-d alignments/auto alignments
Print status sheets
Make custom paper settings
Perform power cleanings
Set the printer clock
Set media counter settings

faqs.question: Why are only matte media types displayed in the driver's media list?
faqs.answer: When matte black ink is installed in the printer, only matte media types are displayed in the driver list. The complete media list appears only when the photo black ink cartridge is installed.

faqs.question: What is the Epson Advanced Black & White Printing Mode?
faqs.answer: This is a proprietary Epson screening and color management technology designed specifically to produce professional level black and white prints. The math behind this unique screen technology takes advantage of our three level black technology along with Yellow, Light Cyan, and Light Magenta to produce professional black and white prints from either color or grayscale files. Epson's Advanced Black and White printing technology is simply another tool or alternative for professionals to use towards achieving the ultimate black and white print.

faqs.question: What is the High Speed setting in the Epson driver?
faqs.answer:
When
High Speed
is selected, the print head prints in both directions to speed up printing. When
High Speed
is deselected or turned off, the printer prints in one direction only, which produces the highest quality images, but slows down printing.

Advanced B&W Photo

.
Restart the computer.

faqs.question: Do I need a raster image processor (RIP) to print from Adobe Illustrator?
faqs.answer:
For the best output, a RIP should be used. Adobe Illustrator is a postscript application that requires a RIP to translate the postscript language. The printer comes with a non-postscript driver that has difficulty translating the postscript language.
Epson has partnered with the following manufacturers for some printers:
ColorBurst
efi
Onyx
Wasatch

faqs.question: Do I need a raster image processor (RIP) to print from Adobe Photoshop?
faqs.answer: No, Adobe Photoshop is not a postscript application and does not require a RIP.

faqs.question: I hear a grinding noise when I turn on my product. What should I do?
faqs.answer:

faqs.question: How do I get service for my product I purchased in another country?
faqs.answer: Due to differences in products sold in other countries, printers need to be serviced in the country of origin.

faqs.question: Which connection enables my product to operate at full speed?
faqs.answer: Both built-in USB (USB port on your computer must be 2.0 compatible) and Ethernet connections allow the printer to operate at full print engine speed. Your CPU is the biggest factor in print engine speed.

faqs.question: Is there an optional TUMI cover available for my product?
faqs.answer: Yes. A custom, fitted printer cover (C4800TUMI) for your printer is available for purchase from the Epson Store.

faqs.question: Does Epson have a program where I can donate my working electronic equipment?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Epson America, Inc. and
Digitunity
have joined together with the goal of helping those who are facing economic challenges or have a disability to gain access to today's technology. With your donation, you not only help the environment, but you also help change the lives of those who need these products the most.
